draft.title: Comparing data with parallel box plots
card: To compare groups, look at the same variable in each group. Parallel box plots sit on one scale, one above the other.
Compare the medians. Example: group A has median 62 and group B has median 55. Group A is centred 7 higher.
Compare the IQRs. A larger IQR means the middle half of the data is more spread out. Example: A has IQR 10 and B has IQR 18, so B is more spread out.
Write the comparison in context, using both centre and spread. You can compare ranges from the whisker ends, but take care, as one extreme value can stretch a range.

3.alt: Parallel box plots on one scale. Group A: median 62, box from 57 to 67 (IQR 10), whiskers from 45 to 78. Group B: median 55, box from 46 to 64 (IQR 18), whiskers from 35 to 80. A is centred higher, and B is more spread out.

draft.remember: Compare medians for centre and IQRs for spread, in context.

a.q: Two parallel box plots show test marks. Class P has median 70 and IQR 8. Class Q has median 70 and IQR 20. Which comparison is best?
opts: Same centre, but Q's scores are more spread out
Same centre, but P's scores are more spread out
Q has a higher centre and a wider spread
P has a higher centre and a narrower spread
a.why: Both medians are 70, so the centres are the same. Q's IQR of 20 is larger than P's IQR of 8, so Q is more spread out. Saying P is more spread out reverses what a larger IQR means.
a.clue: Compare the medians first, then the IQRs.

b.q: Parallel box plots show daily sales (in dollars) at two Geelong cafés. Café X: median 400, IQR 120, range 500. Café Y: median 360, IQR 200, range 380. Using medians and IQRs, which comparison is correct?
opts: X is centred higher, and Y is more spread out
X is centred higher, and X is more spread out
Y is centred higher, and Y is more spread out
Y is centred higher, and X is more spread out
b.why: X's median of 400 is higher than Y's 360, so X is centred higher. Y's IQR of 200 is larger than X's 120, so Y's middle half is more spread out. X's larger range is tempting, but one extreme day can stretch the range.
b.clue: Ignore the ranges and compare the IQRs.

a.best: Same centre, but Q's scores are more spread out

b.best: X is centred higher, and Y is more spread out
